items.title: Machete-wielding mob attacks health workers responding to Ebola in Congo
items.description: Angry youths armed with machetes attacked two community health workers raising ​awareness about the Ebola outbreak in eastern Congo, killing one and wounding the other, according to officials and ‌a memo seen by Reuters on Monday, in the latest in a series of attacks fueled by misinformation. The worker who was killed was an experienced nurse who had worked at the general hospital in the town of Bafwasende in Tshopo province, and was recently tasked with helping to ​raise awareness about the deadly virus in the local community, where he was a well-known figure, a local official ​, and the memo said. “We are shocked at how the population turned against this nurse. It is ⁠impossible to believe that he was mistaken for a stranger,” a local health official told Reuters. The attack took place on Friday ​afternoon, when the nurse and a colleague, a teacher also working on community outreach, stopped to check on a lot of ​land. A group building a home next door began accusing them of spreading the disease by contaminating water. “Here are the people that are spreading the Ebola virus through people’s toilets and rivers!” they shouted, according to the memo shared by a health official. The angry group was ​joined by youths wielding machetes and batons, who attacked the pair. The nurse died on the spot before the hospital’s ​emergency services could reach them, the memo said, while the teacher survived. MISINFORMATION FUELING ATTACK Tshopo is among eight provinces in Congo that are battling a ‌fast-spreading outbreak of the Bundibugyo species of the Ebola virus. Congo’s public health institute reported 9,964 confirmed cases and a 48.6% fatality rate since the outbreak was declared in May. Attacks on health workers have targeted hospitals , vehicles and staff involved in the Ebola response, underscoring the challenge of building trust among the population. The local official said health workers in Bafwasende, where the latest ​attack took place, are sheltering at ​the general hospital under ⁠police guard, too afraid to go home, while the army also briefly deployed to the area. “None of the nurses has slept at their homes because they fear for their security,” the official ​added. Only days earlier, an angry mob attacked another community worker raising awareness about Ebola, and ​set his house ⁠on fire, the memo said. Reuters previously reported on how the rapid spread of health misinformation posed a threat to healthcare workers in eastern Congo even before Ebola began to spread, with multiple health workers killed in Tshopo after they were accused of spreading an imaginary disease ⁠that caused ​male genitals to atrophy. “The killing of a nurse yesterday in Bafwasende is ​a loss to the Ebola response and an even greater loss to patients,” Julien Harneis, the senior United Nations Ebola coordinator, said in a post on ​X on Sunday.

items.title: Regional trade deficit widens sharply
items.description: ISLAMABAD: Pakistan’s trade deficit with nine neighbouring countries widened by 26.62 per cent to $4.97 billion during the first quarter of 2026-27 compared to $3.93bn in the corresponding period last year. The widening gap reflects a contraction in Pakistan’s exports to regional markets, largely due to reduced shipments to Afghanistan and Bangladesh. Trade with Afghanistan, including exports, has remained suspended since Oct 10, 2025, further weighing on overall export performance. Imports from China rose sharply during the July-September quarter, contributing significantly to the widening imbalance. Consequently, the bilateral deficit with China widened by $858.808 million, accounting for approximately 82.18pc of the increase in the combined deficit with the nine countries. Gap with nine neighbours rises 26.6pc to $4.97bn in July-September Exports to China rose marginally, while exports to Nepal also grew in percentage terms, though the increase remained negligible in dollar value. In contrast, shipments to Afghanistan, Bangladesh and Sri Lanka declined, according to the latest data compiled by the State Bank of Pakistan. Exports to nine countries—Afghanistan, China, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, India, Iran, Nepal, Bhutan and the Maldives—fell 6.72pc to $944.24mn in July to September of FY27, down from $1.01 billion in the same period last year. By contrast, imports surged 19.79pc to $5.92bn in 3MFY27 from $4.94bn in the same months of the previous fiscal year. Further analysis showed that imports from China grew 19.76pc to $5.82bn in 3MFY27, up from $4.85bn over the same period last year. Pakistan’s exports to China grew 17.95pc to $663.57m in 3MFY27 from $562.56m in the same months of the preceding fiscal year. Imports from India increased by 68.90pc to $61.74m in 3MFY27 from $36.55m over the last year. Meanwhile, no exports to India were recorded in the first quarter of FY27. Exports to Afghanistan fell 88.34pc to $18.86m in 3MFY27, down from $161.76m last year. Imports stood at $0.25m in 3MFY27, compared with $4.52m in FY26, a decline of 94.40pc. Pakistan’s exports to Bangladesh declined by 2.96pc to $174.77m in 3MFY27 from $180.12m over the last year. Imports dipped 36.11pc to $13.88m in 3MFY27 from $21.73m over the last year. Published in Dawn, October 27th, 2026

items.title: 3ᵉ Sommet Russie-Afrique à Moscou : Le Premier ministre Jean Emmanuel Ouédraogo porte la voix de la souveraineté burkinabè
items.description: Ayant quitté Ouagadougou ce lundi 26 octobre 2026, le Premier ministre, le Camarade Rimtalba Jean Emmanuel Ouédraogo, représente le Président du Faso, le Capitaine Ibrahim Traoré, au troisième Sommet Russie–Afrique et au Forum économique et humanitaire organisés les 28 et 29 octobre à Moscou. Face au Président russe Vladimir Poutine et aux dirigeants du continent africain, la délégation burkinabè entend défendre une vision axée sur la transformation locale des ressources, la maîtrise technologique et le renforcement de la souveraineté économique et sécuritaire de la Nation. Dans la continuité des rencontres de Sotchi en 2019 et de Saint-Pétersbourg en 2023, la capitale de la Fédération de Russie accueille, ces 28 et 29 octobre 2026, les travaux du troisième Sommet Russie–Afrique. À la tête de la délégation nationale, le Premier ministre, Chef du Gouvernement, le Camarade Rimtalba Jean Emmanuel Ouédraogo, y porte le message du Président du Faso, le Capitaine Ibrahim Traoré. Aux côtés du Président russe Vladimir Poutine et des dirigeants africains, cette grande réunion permettra d'évaluer le plan d'action 2023-2026 et d'adopter une nouvelle déclaration ainsi qu'une feuille de route stratégique pour la période 2027-2029. Au-delà des thématiques classiques du commerce, des investissements, de la sécurité alimentaire et de la défense de la souveraineté des États, le Forum économique et humanitaire qui accompagne le sommet explore des secteurs d'avenir. Les discussions couvrent notamment le développement industriel, les transferts de technologies, la transformation numérique, l'intelligence artificielle, ainsi que les applications pacifiques de l'énergie nucléaire. Les volets sociaux relatifs à la santé, à l'éducation et à la formation professionnelle figurent également au cœur de l'agenda des concertations. Au nom du Chef de l'État, le Premier ministre défend des objectifs précis destinés à renforcer les capacités productives nationales. Le Burkina Faso vise l'émergence de projets concrets axés sur la transformation industrielle sur place des matières premières, l'appropriation des compétences technologiques et la qualification de la jeunesse. Pour l'exécutif burkinabè, l'industrialisation locale et la maîtrise du savoir-faire constituent les leviers indispensables à la conquête d'une véritable autonomie économique. En marge des assemblées plénières, le Chef du Gouvernement conduit une série d'entretiens bilatéraux et d'audiences de travail pour sceller de nouveaux accords. Cette mission s'inscrit dans la dynamique de rapprochement matérialisée par la signature, le 12 février 2026, de l'Accord sur les fondements des relations entre le Burkina Faso et la Fédération de Russie. Elle traduit la politique de diversification des partenariats internationaux menée par les autorités de la Transition, dans le respect de la souveraineté nationale, de l'égalité et des intérêts réciproques. items.title: Énergie solaire et agriculture : Le Burkina Faso et le FMI explorent de nouvelles pistes de financement stratégique
items.description: Ce lundi 26 octobre 2026 à Ouagadougou, la Ministre déléguée chargée du Budget, Fatoumata Bako/Traoré, a reçu en audience une délégation du Fonds monétaire international (FMI) menée par Jaroslaw Wieczorek, chef de mission pour le Burkina Faso. Au cœur de cette rencontre figuraient l'évaluation des perspectives économiques nationales, la poursuite du programme économique et financier conjoint, ainsi que le financement stratégique de l'énergie solaire et de l'agriculture. Saluant la croissance économique et la rigueur dans la gestion de la dette publique, l'institution financière internationale a réaffirmé son soutien aux réformes budgétaires du pays. Les échanges économiques de haut niveau se poursuivent dans la capitale burkinabè. La Ministre déléguée chargée du Budget, Fatoumata Bako/Traoré, a accordé ce lundi 26 octobre 2026 une audience officielle à une délégation du Fonds monétaire international (FMI). Conduite par le chef de mission pour le Burkina Faso, Jaroslaw Wieczorek, cette rencontre s'inscrit dans le cadre du dialogue régulier sur la gouvernance financière et le cadrage macroéconomique du pays. Au cours des discussions, les deux parties ont abordé en profondeur les enjeux majeurs liés à la gestion des finances publiques et aux prévisions économiques nationales. Outre les questions strictement budgétaires, la réunion a permis d'examiner les perspectives de poursuite du programme économique et financier conclu entre le Burkina Faso et le FMI. Les échanges ont également ouvert des pistes prometteuses quant aux possibilités de financement des secteurs stratégiques, avec une priorité accordée à l'énergie solaire et à l'agriculture, deux leviers majeurs pour la souveraineté et le développement durable du pays. À l'issue de l'audience, le chef de mission du FMI, Jaroslaw Wieczorek, s'est félicité de la dynamique de croissance économique observée au Burkina Faso. Le responsable onusien a particulièrement salué les efforts soutenus déployés par le gouvernement burkinabè en matière de gestion de la dette publique. Selon le FMI, ces avancées témoignent de la volonté ferme des autorités de consolider les équilibres macroéconomiques et d'assurer une gestion rigoureuse des deniers publics. Trump invokes 9/11 in urging voters to oppose El-Sayed
items.description: Senator Bernie Sanders joins hands with Democrat senatorial candidate Abdul El-Sayed at a campaign rally in Grand Rapids, Michigan.—AFP PORT HURON: President Donald Trump at a Sunday campaign rally ratcheted up his push to link US Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed to Muslim extremists, comparing him to the 9/11 attackers while saying Democrats would let violent anti-American terrorists into the United States. “I’m here to keep a jihadist, Muslim Brotherhood member from becoming a United States senator,” the president told a receptive audience in Port Huron, which is in a Michigan area where 66pc of the vote went to Trump in the 2024 presidential election. If El-Sayed wins, he would be the first Muslim elected to the US Senate. Trump has sought to paint him as an anti-American Muslim radical, and on Sunday he took the rhetoric to a new level, likening El-Sayed to the attackers who took over United Flight 93 during the Sept 11, 2001, attacks. Michigan has one of the nation’s most competitive US Senate contests going into the Nov 3 midterm elections, with former US Representative Mike Rogers, a Republican, and El-Sayed vying for an open seat that will help to decide control of the chamber. The president on Sunday compared voting against El-Sayed to the actions of Michigan native Todd Bea­mer and others who fought back aga­i­­nst the Flight 93 hijackers. “Twenty-five years later, Michigan needs to stand up and fight, just like Todd did, to stop a jihadist from walking into the Capitol,” said Trump. If El-Sayed wins, “he would be the only senator that will have to go through a metal detector before he’s allowed to go in the Senate,” Trump said. El-Sayed has dismissed the accusations against him, and at a Sunday night event, he suggested that Trump’s frequent emphasis of El-Sayed’s name contains a measure of hypocrisy. “I get that the president of the United States takes personal offence to my first name,” El-Sayed told an audience in Grand Rapids, Michigan. “He doesn’t mind as much when it’s a shared name from the Saudis who are funding his son-in-law’s private equity, doesn’t seem to mind as much when it’s the Qataris who are giving him a $400 million private jet.” Affinity Partners, Trump son-in-law Jared Kushner’s investment fund, has reportedly received billions from a Saudi Government entity. Qatar gifted Trump a Boeing 747 jet. The mostly White crowd at Sunday’s rally cheered Trump’s comments on El-Sayed. Some attendees yelled traitor and others yelled deport, although El-Sayed was born in Michigan. Terrance Camburn, a 52-year-old disabled Army veteran from Sandusky, Michigan, said he supported Trump’s criticism because of El-Sayed’s political beliefs. “I’ve been down to Dearborn and I’ve seen many of the things he agrees with,” Camburn said when asked about Trump’s 9/11 comments. Dearborn, Michigan, has the highest per-capita concentration of Muslims of any US city. As he left the venue after the rally, Rogers did not respond to questions about Trump’s invocation of 9/11. But earlier on Sunday, he said on NBC’s “Meet the Press” that he did not agree with the notion that El-Sayed is a violent terrorist. “I’ve never called him a terrorist,” Rogers told NBC. Rogers has alleged without evidence that El Sayed has ties to the Muslim Broth­erhood, one of the Arab world’s oldest and most influential Islamist groups. El-Sayed has denied affiliation with the Muslim Brotherhood, saying it is “shameful” for Rogers to question his allegiance to the United States. Rogers told “Meet the Press” that El-Sayed had not sufficiently responded to questions about the allegations. “He’s a Democrat Socialist of America-aligned candidate who has these pretty radical support groups that don’t like America,” he said. Trump’s speech in eastern Michigan on Sunday came a day after former President Barack Obama campaigned for Democrats in the state, underscoring its importance in next week’s elections. At a Saturday rally in Detroit, Obama framed the attacks by El-Sayed’s opponents as an attempt to make him look “less American than they are.” The former president compared them to his own experience as the target of false claims that he was born in Kenya. “This stuff didn’t work on me,” Obama said. “Not in Michigan. It’s not going to work on Abdul.” Dem­­ocrats need to gain just a handful of seats each in the US Senate and House of Repr­esentatives to overturn Repu­blicans’ narrow 53-47 and 218-214 majorities. Published in Dawn, October 27th, 2026

items.title: Balochistan Assembly shelves resolution against Sardari system
items.description: • Speaker says legislation abolishing the system already passed in 1976, applies to whole country • JI MPA and opposition leader trade barbs over renewed move to abolish system QUETTA: A resolution seeking the immediate abolition of the Sardari system in Balo­ch­istan and a ban on the use of the titles Sardar and Nawab in writing and speech was dispo­sed of in the provincial assembly on Monday. The agenda for the session included a resolution moved by Jamaat-i-Islami MPA Hidayatur Rehman Baloch seeking the abolition of the Sardari system in the province. However, Speaker retired Captain Abdul Khaliq Achakzai informed the house that a review of the available legal and judicial record showed that legislation abolishing the Sardari system had already been passed and implemented in 1976 and applied to the entire country. He also noted that the Balochistan High Court had issued decisions on the Sardari system, which were upheld by the Federal Constitutional Court on March 6 this year. In view of the existing legal and judicial position, the speaker disposed of the resolution. Speaking on a point of objection later, Mr Rehman said the resolution had been included in the agenda and that he would make the necessary corrections before presenting it again. Heated exchange An exchange of taunts between Mr Rehman and Opposition Leader Mir Younis Aziz Zehri followed, with treasury members also speaking in support of the opposition leader. Rising on a point of order, Mr Zehri said the matter could no longer be discussed beca­use the speaker had already disposed of the resolution. Mr Rehman retorted by asking why the opposition was offended by his remarks. A heated exchange of sarcastic and harsh comments ensued between the two members. Parliamentary Secretary Agha Umer Ahmedzai said the Sardari system had existed for thousands of years and argued that it was not for an individual to declare the entire system wrong. “If someone commits oppression or injustice somewhere, it should be pointed out. It is not right to blame all Sardars,” he said. Parliamentary Secretary Nawabzada Zarain Khan Magsi argued that the matter should not be discussed further as the resolution had been disposed of. “If someone wants to talk about it, he should bring a resolution again in the assembly,” he said. The speaker said he had disposed of the resolution but added that Mr Rehman’s point should be heard, as the JI MPA was seeking implementation of the legislation enacted to abolish the Sardari system. However, the speaker adjourned the session until Nov 10 due to a lack of quorum. Published in Dawn, October 27th, 2026

items.title: Carnet noir du cinéma panafricain : L’acteur et réalisateur burkinabè Wabinlé Nabié s’est éteint à 53 ans
items.description: Le cinéma et le théâtre burkinabè ainsi que la scène artistique panafricaine sont en deuil. Né en 1973 à Fafo (Burkina Faso), l'acteur, réalisateur et comédien Wabinlé Nabié est décédé brutalement le samedi 24 octobre 2026 à Malakoff, en région parisienne, à l'âge de 53 ans. Formé à l'Atelier Théâtre Burkinabè (ATB) et au Carrefour International de Théâtre de Ouagadougou (CITO), cet artiste polyvalent s'était illustré aussi bien dans des séries télévisées populaires que dans des longs-métrages de renommée internationale et des projets documentaires engagés. Il laisse derrière lui une œuvre remarquable marquée par la préservation de la mémoire et des traditions africaines. Le monde de la culture et du 7ᵉ art est frappé par une triste nouvelle. L'acteur, réalisateur et comédien burkinabè Wabinlé Nabié s'est éteint brutalement le samedi 24 octobre 2026 à Malakoff, en région parisienne, à l'âge de 53 ans, selon des informations confirmées par ses proches. Né en 1973 à Fafo, au Burkina Faso, l'artiste s'était imposé au fil des décennies comme une figure incontournable du théâtre et du cinéma panafricain, consacrant sa vie au rayonnement de la création culturelle. Formé initialement à l'école de l'Atelier Théâtre Burkinabè (ATB) puis au sein du Carrefour International de Théâtre de Ouagadougou (CITO), Wabinlé Nabié a bâti une carrière prolifique s'étendant sur le continent africain et en Europe. Le grand public conserve le souvenir de son talent dans des séries télévisées populaires telles que Waga Love , Le Petit Sergent , Cour commune , ou plus récemment la série française Nona et ses filles (2020). Sur grand écran, il s'est illustré sous la direction de grands cinéastes dans des longs-métrages notables comme La raison du plus fort de Missa Hébié, Cessez-le-feu d'Emmanuel Courcol, La vie pour de vrai de Dany Boon, Gueules Noires , L'Histoire de Souleymane de Boris Lojkine (2023), ainsi que La nuit du destin (2026). Au-delà de son jeu d'acteur, Wabinlé Nabié s'était affirmé comme un réalisateur exigeant avec son film documentaire marquant Les Scarifiés . À travers cette œuvre intime et anthropologique, il explorait sa propre identité en documentant les scarifications de son ethnie, les Bwaba, une tradition ancestrale aujourd'hui en voie de disparition. Avant son rappel à Dieu, le cinéaste travaillait activement sur un ambitieux projet de film historique intitulé Wisin le père voltaïque , dédié à la figure politique de Daniel Ouezzin Coulibaly. Il laisse le souvenir d'un homme de culture profondément attaché à la sauvegarde de la mémoire et du patrimoine national. items.title: Completion ceremony held for renovated CPV martyrs' cemetery in DPRK
items.description: A completion ceremony for the renovation project for Chinese People's Volunteers (CPV) martyrs' cemeteries was held Saturday in Sinphyong County, North Hwanghae Province of the Democratic People's Republic of Korea (DPRK), on the occasion of the 76th anniversary of the CPV's entry into the DPRK to fight in the War to Resist US Aggression and Aid Korea. The ceremony started at around 10 a.m. (0100 GMT) with the national anthems of China and the DPRK. Representatives from China and the DPRK laid flower baskets for the CPV martyrs, stood in silent tribute, presented flowers and poured liquor in remembrance, and visited the martyrs' tombs and the wall of martyrs' names to pay profound respect. Qi Han, charge d'affaires ad interim of the Chinese Embassy in the DPRK, said that 76 years ago, the CPV fought shoulder to shoulder with the DPRK army and people, shared weal and woe, and the traditional China-DPRK friendship forged in blood will never fade. China stands ready to continue to work with the DPRK to implement the important consensus reached by the top leaders of the two parties and the two countries, do well in honoring and commemorating the CPV martyrs in the DPRK, consolidate traditional bonds of ties, enhance strategic coordination, maintain regional peace, honor the martyrs who sacrificed their lives and benefit the two peoples via peace and development, Qi said. Hong Zongming, vice minister of China's Ministry of Veterans Affairs, said the memorial facilities for the CPV martyrs in the DPRK are "an important platform" for carrying forward the spirit of the fallen heroes and the China-DPRK friendship. Calling the protection and management of the memorial facilities "a lofty cause passed down from generation to generation," Kang Chol Ho, vice minister of the Ministry of Urban Management of the DPRK, said the undertaking is dedicated to carrying forward the great spirit of the CPV fighters demonstrated in the war. The DPRK side will work with the Chinese side to continue doing relevant work well and make positive contributions to inheriting and promoting the traditional friendship, he said. In late October 2025, China and the DPRK held a groundbreaking ceremony in Sinphyong County for the renovation project. As of this month, the renovation has been completed at five CPV martyrs' cemeteries in the DPRK, through joint efforts by relevant Chinese and DPRK departments and agencies. (Cover: A completion ceremony for the renovation project for Chinese People's Volunteers martyrs' cemeteries is held in Sinphyong County, North Hwanghae Province, Democratic People's Republic of Korea, October 24, 2026. /CMG )

items.title: Concours national de dissertation 2026 : La Fondation UBA récompense les meilleurs candidats après une mobilisation de plus de 1 000 participants
items.description: À l’issue d’une compétition intellectuelle d’envergure nationale ayant mobilisé plus de 1000 candidats à travers le Burkina Faso, la Fondation United Bank for Africa (UBA) a récompensé les lauréats de la première édition de son concours de dissertation, le National Essay Competition (NEC), lors d’une cérémonie organisée le vendredi 23 octobre 2026 au siège de la banque à Ouagadougou. Invités à réfléchir sur la transformation digitale de l’école burkinabè, les élèves ont rivalisé d’argumentation et de maturité. C’est l’élève Tassnim Idrissou, du Prytanée militaire de Kadiogo (PMK), qui s’est hissée sur la plus haute marche du podium, emportant le premier prix, composé d’un chèque d’un million de francs CFA, d’une attestation, d’un sac UBA et d’une moto neuve. Lancée le 17 avril 2026 par la Fondation UBA, la première édition du National Essay Competition (NEC) s’est donné pour mission de stimuler la réflexion et le goût de la recherche chez les jeunes. Ouvert aux élèves âgés de moins de 18 ans, de la classe de seconde à la terminale, issus d’établissements publics et privés, le concours s’est emparé d’une thématique au cœur des enjeux nationaux : « L’école burkinabè face à la transformation digitale : doit-on repenser la stratégie d’éducation nationale ? » . Cet appel à la réflexion a suscité un engouement remarquable, concrétisé par la réception de 1 256 copies transmises par e-mail et via un formulaire en ligne. Après une première phase de correction qui a permis de retenir 760 copies conformes, le jury a sélectionné huit finalistes pour une épreuve décisive en présentiel (sept au siège de UBA à Ouagadougou et un à Bobo-Dioulasso). Selon le barème établi, la note de la première étape comptait pour 30 % de la moyenne finale et celle du présentiel pour 70 %. Tassnim Idrissou sacrée sur le podium de l’excellence La cérémonie de remise des prix, organisée le vendredi 23 octobre 2026 au siège de l’institution bancaire, a réuni la directrice générale de UBA Burkina, Rasmata Djibo, ses collaborateurs, ainsi que les encadreurs et les familles des lauréats. C’est Tassnim Idrissou, élève en classe de terminale A4 au Prytanée militaire de Kadiogo (PMK), qui s’est classée à la première place. Elle a reçu une récompense d’un montant de 1 000 000 de francs CFA, une attestation de félicitations, un sac UBA et une moto neuve. Le deuxième prix est revenu à Aron Clauvis Yempabou Ouoba, du Lycée scientifique régional de Bobo-Dioulasso, crédité d’un chèque de 750 000 FCFA, d’une attestation, d’un sac et d’une moto. La troisième position a été décrochée par Estelle Ingrid Tégwendé Nana, du Lycée scientifique national de Ouagadougou, qui repart avec 500 000 FCFA, une attestation, un sac ainsi qu’une moto. Saluant la persévérance de l’ensemble des finalistes, la Fondation UBA a offert une moto neuve à chacun des cinq autres lauréats. Investir dans la jeunesse et cultiver l’esprit critique Dans son allocution, la directrice générale de UBA Burkina, Rasmata Djibo, a souligné que cet événement célèbre le mérite, le travail et la rigueur intellectuelle de la jeunesse. Rappelant qu’« investir dans l’éducation, c’est investir dans l’avenir de notre pays », la responsable a mis en avant les vertus de la dissertation, un exercice qui enseigne à structurer sa pensée, à écouter la diversité des points de vue et à exercer un sens critique indispensable dans la vie citoyenne. De son côté, la grande gagnante Tassnim Idrissou a exprimé sa fierté d’avoir relevé ce défi, qui lui a permis de se dépasser, invitant chaleureusement ses camarades lycéens à participer massivement aux prochaines éditions. Le Ballon d’Or brille, l’Afrique dort!
items.description: Alea jacta est! Les Ballon d’Or 2026 sont connus et s’appellent Harry Kane, pour les hommes et Alexia Putellas, pour les femmes! Ils ont été célébrés au bout d’un vote et d’une annonce à suspense, ce soir du lundi 26 octobre 2026. L’Anglais a remporté le graal du football européen, devant le goleador français Kylian Mbappé, et le plus jeune talent, l’Espagnol Lamine Yamal. Mais, aux dires des spécialistes et autres bookmakers du ballon rond, tous les trois joueurs qui ont enflammé les stades européens durant l’année écoulée, méritaient le trophée. Sauf que, comme le football, qui sait être autant cruel que magnifique, a encore fait des siennes. Et tant pis pour les magiques «Numéro 10» du Real de Madrid et du FC Barcelone qui, à l’ouvrage, devront se remettre, pour essayer de décrocher ce titre tant convoité. A peine le vainqueur dévoilé, la compétition est donc déjà relancée, et se déroulera, soit avec les mêmes acteurs, soit animée par de nouvelles pépites qui n’attendent que leur heure. Le prochain Ballon d’Or sera-t-il Africain? Rien n’est moins sûr, mais c’est une interrogation qui s’invite, malheureusement, très peu dans le débat, depuis le sacre, en 1995, du Libérien George Weah, le premier, et jusque-là, seul Africain, Ballon d’Or européen. Mister George, dans sa dynamique de premier est, du reste, le premier footballeur devenu chef de l’Etat sur le continent, dans son pays le Liberia. La parenthèse présidentielle fermée, et celle du Ballon d’Or réouverte, l’Afrique, malgré tous ses talents qui soulèvent les foules dans les plus grands championnats européens, n’a jamais pu soulever, une deuxième fois, le trophée qui fait courir tous les footballeurs. Et alors que l’Afrique dort derrière le Ballon d'Or, les Africains d’origine, eux s’illustrent, fort admirablement, dans ce concours. Zinedine Zidane, Karim Benzema, Ousmane Dembélé, ont, ainsi, connu les honneurs de cette distinction, tout comme Kylian Mbappé était à un chouïa du sacre cette année. Mais tous non comme, respectivement, Algériens pour les deux premiers, Malien pour le troisième et Camerounais pour le quatrième, mais en tant que Français! Pourtant, les Ballons d’Or du football européen, il y en a eu, depuis la création de la compétition en 1956. Et tous ont eu comme coéquipiers, de grands footballeurs africains comme Roger Milla, Salif Keïta «Domingo», Laurent Pokou, Aboubacar Titi Camara, Abedi Ayew Pelé, Samuel Eto'o Fils, Didier Drogba, Sadio Mané, Mohamed Salah, pour ne citer que ceux-ci. Ces Africains n’ont-ils pas assez brillé sur les stades européens pour mériter le Ballon d’Or? Certes, l’Afrique possède aussi son concours de Ballon d’Or, mais les meilleurs Africains sont sociétaires de ces grands clubs européens où ils ont exporté la magie du football africain. Et à ce titre, ils doivent bien pouvoir êtres régulièrement nominés, et parfois mériter le Ballon d’Or. Même si tous ne réunissent pas les critères de ce jeu, d’ailleurs souvent flous et contestés comme tel, certains joueurs africains, qui font briller le football européen, peuvent bien prétendre à la récompense au titre de laquelle ils sont rarement, ou jamais associés, en dehors du miracle de 1995 avec le Libérien du Milan AC, George Weah! Vivement un successeur pour Mister George, afin que l’Afrique ne dorme plus au Ballon d’Or! Par Wakat Séra L’article Le Ballon d’Or brille, l’Afrique dort! est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .

items.title: Domaine du génie civil : L’ordre des ingénieurs en génie civil veille à la bonne pratique de la profession
items.description: L'ordre des Ingénieurs en Génie Civil du Burkina Faso (OIGC-BF) a réuni la presse autour d’un déjeuner le vendredi 23 octobre 2026, à Ouagadougou. Le Conseil de l’Ordre est revenu au cours de la rencontre sur l’exercice en terme légal de la profession d’ingénieur en génie civil. Il a mis aussi en garde ceux qui exerce le métier sans inscription au tableau de l’Ordre. Le presse a été appelé à aider à mieux faire connaître les missions de l'Ordre. Pour cette rencontre, le conseil de l'ordre a axé son intervention au tour du thème au cœur de la qualité des constructions : la responsabilité des ingénieurs en génie civil ». Ousmane Honoré Ouedraogo, président du conseil de l'ordre, a dans rendu un hommage bien appuyé aux ingénieurs en génie civil du Burkina Faso. Dans les bureaux d’études, sur les chantiers, dans les laboratoires et les services de contrôle, ils travaillent souvent dans des conditions difficiles, parfois au prix de grands sacrifices. Leur travail est discret, mais il est partout >> indique le président Ouedraogo. Pour Ousmane Honoré Ouedraogo, la responsabilité des ingénieurs en génie civil s'exerce à chaque étape. À savoir les études et les calculs jusqu’au contrôle de l’exécution et à la réception. Et pour arriver à un ouvrage de qualité, il faut de la rigueur. Construire reste une œuvre collective, qui engage maîtres d’ouvrage, ingénieurs, entreprises, laboratoires et services de contrôle >> soutient l’ingénieur Ousmane Honoré Ouedraogo. Dans sa déclaration, Ousmane Honoré Ouedraogo s'est appuyé sur les textes législatifs qui guident la profession. Et selon le code de l’urbanisme et de la construction adopté en 2026, l'importance de l’intervention de professionnels qualifiés et habilités est exigé. C’est pour cela que l’ingénieur Ouedraogo invite les maîtres d’ouvrage publics et privés, les promoteurs et les particuliers à ne plus considérer les études techniques et le suivi-contrôle comme des dépenses accessoires. L’exercice de notre profession, la loi n° 020-2012/AN du 10 mai 2012 est sans ambiguïté. Son article 8 dispose que nul ne peut exercer la profession d’ingénieur en génie civil au Burkina Faso s’il n’est inscrit au tableau de l’Ordre. Son article 68 qualifie d’exercice illégal le fait d’exercer sans cette inscription ou, pour l’ingénieur-conseil, sans police d’assurance valide >> rappelle le président du conseil de l'ordre. Les sanctions à cette infraction est sans commentaire. En effet, l’article 69 prévoit une peine d’emprisonnement d’un (01) à cinq (05) ans et une amende de 300 000 à 1 500 000 francs CFA, ou l’une de ces deux peines seulement, assorties le cas échéant de la fermeture de l’établissement, de la confiscation ou de l’exclusion des marchés publics. D'autres amendes sont édictées à l’article 70. L’article 71 quant à lui, donne quitus à l’OIGC-BF de faire constater ces infractions sur les chantiers et de saisir les juridictions pénales. Le Conseil prend l’engagement de lutter contre l’exercice illégal de la profession, de faire aboutir la tarification des prestations des ingénieurs, de moderniser leur textes de base, de renforcer l’encadrement des stagiaires, former ses membres, et d'accompagner l’Etat en participant aux travaux de normalisation et cadres de réflexion. Le secteur du bâtiment est complexe, c’est pourquoi l'ordre se dit prêt à accompagner les professionnels des médias pour une information exacte qui protège les populations. L'an prochain, l'OIGC-BF sera très heureuse d’accueillir le Mal et le Niger pour un partage de savoirs, de l’innovation et de normes adaptées à aux réalités sahéliennes. Jean Narcisse KOUDOU L’article Domaine du génie civil : L'ordre des ingénieurs en génie civil veille à la bonne pratique de la profession est apparu en premier sur NetAfrique.net .

items.title: Construction : les ventes de ciment repartent à la hausse à fin septembre
items.description: Les ventes de ciment se sont accrues de 1,2% au terme des neuf premiers mois de 2026, après un affermissement de 10,6% un an auparavant, selon la Direction des études et des prévisions financières (DEPF). Cette évolution est portée notamment par le renforcement des ventes du segment du béton prêt à l’emploi (+8,6%), conjugué à la croissance soutenue des livraisons du segment de l’infrastructure (+19,5%) et, dans une moindre mesure, à la hausse de 0,9% de celles du bâtiment, indique la DEPF dans sa récente note de conjoncture. La valeur ajoutée du secteur de construction s’est accrue de 2,8% au deuxième trimestre et de 1,5% au premier trimestre, pour clôturer le premier semestre 2026 sur une hausse moyenne de 2,1%, en ralentissement par rapport à la hausse notable enregistrée un an plus tôt (+7,4%). Cette tendance positive devrait se maintenir au troisième trimestre 2026, comme en témoigne la hausse de 5,4% des ventes de ciment, principal baromètre de l’activité du secteur, après une augmentation de 8% au deuxième trimestre et une baisse de 10,9% au premier trimestre 2026. Il est à noter que les ventes observées au troisième trimestre ont atteint un niveau record, par rapport aux treize dernières années. items.title: Le Niger accuse le Tchad d’une frappe de drone sur son territoire et saisit l’ONU
items.description: Le gouvernement du Niger accuse N'Djamena d'avoir mené une attaque sur son sol. Dans un communiqué officiel lu à la Radiodiffusion télévision du Niger (RTN) ce 27 octobre 2026, l'exécutif nigérien affirme que le territoire national a été la cible d'une frappe aérienne par drone le 24 octobre vers 1 heure du matin. Selon le communiqué, cette opération aurait été menée depuis le Tchad « avec l'appui d'une puissance étrangère, la France ». Le gouvernement nigérien « tient le Tchad pour entièrement responsable » de cet acte. Pour justifier cette accusation, Niamey soutient que le Tchad s'est inscrit « depuis plusieurs mois » dans une « démarche hostile » et qu'il offrirait « une dimension stratégique à des mercenaires ». En réaction à ces événements, les autorités nigériennes ont annoncé la convocation de l'ambassadeur du Tchad à Niamey ainsi que la saisine officielle des Nations Unies. items.title: How the Campaign War Chests Are Being Spent
items.description: Subscribe here: Apple Podcasts | Spotify | YouTube | Overcast | Pocket Casts In the weeks heading into next week’s midterm election, President Trump has been crisscrossing the country trying to gin up enthusiasm among his base at rallies—where he’s gone on Islamophobic rants and inexplicably praised a candidate’s backside. Meanwhile, spending on races across the country has been through the roof: His super PAC has been pumping hundreds of millions into campaigns to help vulnerable Republicans, as has Elon Musk; and Mike Bloomberg is spending tens of millions to help Democrats. It’s a sprint to the first Tuesday in November. . But enthusiasm is not really the word to describe most Americans’ sentiments heading into this election. Economic concerns about the price of goods such as gas and groceries, an unpopular war with Iran that has driven that rise in everyday costs, and angst from Democrats about an unchecked Trump administration is fueling the conversation ahead of Election Day. This week on Radio Atlantic , my colleagues Ashley Parker and Michael Scherer join me to discuss the closing messages from Democrats and Republicans, the campaign spending blitz, and the issues voters will be taking with them to the polls. The following is a transcript of the episode: Ashley Parker: You may recall, one of the key things Donald Trump promised was no more forever wars, no more quagmires in the Middle East, et cetera, et cetera. And the war in Iran, which people already don’t like on its merit, is so deeply tied with gas prices in a way that people can make that one-to-one connection. So it’s just a nest of what everyone hates. Adam Harris: This is Radio Atlantic , I’m Adam Harris, and we’re a week away from the midterm elections. The stakes have been clear for a while: The election will determine whether President Trump spends his last two years in office with a Congress that continues to allow him to enact his policy agenda with few, if any, checks—or as a lame duck. The president has been zigzagging the country trying to excite his base, as early-voting numbers are already surging well ahead of 2018 and 2022 midterm cycles. My colleagues Ashley Parker and Michael Scherer are with me to discuss the closing messages for Republicans and Democrats, where they’re spending in the last week, and how voters are responding. Let’s get to questions. Welcome back. Ashley Parker: Thank you. Michael Scherer: Yeah, thanks for having me. Harris: Ashley, I want to start with the news that the Justice Department sued to block Senate results if Republicans lose in Alaska. What do we know about what’s happening there? Parker: In Alaska, you have this amusing situation, where you have two candidates named Dan Sullivan. One is the Republican incumbent, and one is an independent. And Republicans and the Justice Department are trying to say that the results may be invalid because of confusion between the two names. They wanna make sure that someone who goes into the voting booth and votes for Dan Sullivan, the independent, actually meant to vote for him and not Dan Sullivan, the Republican. But my understanding, from what legal experts have said, is that this is a ridiculous case that almost certainly will not hold up in court. Scherer: But it does serve the purpose of getting this in the news in Alaska, which is—I think the goal of the case is to elevate it, to make people recognize again, Wait, there are two Dan Sullivans. I gotta figure out which is the right one. It’s also interesting there are races across the country where both parties have been trying to create new parties to get fourth candidates on the ballot, or to take over the Green Party ticket in places to bleed off voters. So that trickery is advancing. Harris: And in Alaska, it’s particularly interesting because it’s ranked-choice voting. So how is that factoring in? Scherer: There’s a lot of Republican education going on now to try and convince people not to put Mary Peltola, the Democrat, as the second person anywhere. So they’re trying to tell their voters, Just do the real Dan Sullivan, one, and then leave the rest blank, because they’re worried on subsequent ballots she’d pull ahead. Harris: There’s been haze over the election that the president might try to contest results elsewhere if Democrats were successful. And I wonder: Is this attempt from the DOJ the sort of foreshadowing of the possibility of the administration contesting the election in other states if things don’t go their way? Parker: That was a point I was gonna make. Michael is right that part of this lawsuit—that, I think, any DOJ lawyer worth their salt knows is not likely to advance or be successful—is helping Republicans in Alaska understand that there is one Republican, Dan Sullivan, and that’s who they should vote for. That’s valuable for Republicans. The flip side is, as you point out, there is a tremendous angst going back to January 6, where Democrats and a lot of the electorate is terrified that Donald Trump and his team will not accept the results of a free and fair election. You talk to the reasonable people in Trump’s inner circle, and they say—and Michael did a great story on this that he can talk about—they say, Yes, there is a contingent in the president’s ear trying to get him to declare martial law, but that’s a very tiny contingent. That’s not what’s gonna happen. But I do think the concern is this shows, for instance, that the Justice Department is willing to go forward with something that is objectively, on its face, according to lawyers, absurd, because the president wants them to do it. Which fairly raises the question: What else might they be willing to do simply because the president wants them to do it? Scherer: I think there’s two categories of things, and the problem is you can’t easily define them ahead of time. One is: You very often have litigation after elections. And so I think there will be races that are close; there will be races where lawsuits are filed, where the DOJ might intervene. But I think the American people can rest assured, at least at the moment—the courts have been almost unanimously rejecting the president’s efforts to intervene in this election. He’s tried five or 10 different ways—stripping voter rolls, banning mail-in ballots, all kinds of things. And the courts have just struck them down consistently. And so I think it’s likely that the litigation that follows a close race will be the way litigations follow[ing] close races have been in the past. Now, the concern that Ashley mentioned is this other idea that the president tries to do something that’s never been done before, which is to declare, say, The election machines are fraudulent and we can’t trust the vote ; or to say, We have to seize these ballots ; or even the martial-law idea. Another concern is that Republicans refuse because of a dispute to seat the winner of a race. So you could have an effort that would have to be litigated and fought, where Republicans try and prevent a Democrat who was elected from taking power next year. And that would be a mess. That said, I think it’s unlikely that that second category of things goes forward right now. And the reason is that there’s very little appetite in the Republican Party, and there’s very little appetite in the senior ranks of the White House. So to do it, the president would have to basically overrule his own advisers and pick a fight with the Republican Party in a way that he probably comes out worse from, not better. And the bottom line is he’s been expecting to lose this race since the beginning of the year. So it’s not like it was in 2020, where his entire reputation, his entire legacy, was on the line. Parker: Right. And I was gonna say, he might be willing—that’s the sort of thing he was clearly, in 2020, willing to do on behalf of himself to try to stay in office for four more years. I don’t know that he’s going to expend that sort of reputational capital for a random House Republican. Scherer: Although, the other thing we should say is it’s certain that, after this election, he’s gonna continue to demand changes to the voting system, and he’s gonna continue to launch investigations into the voting system. And so the noise around this is gonna continue. He wants the voting system we have now changed. And he basically wasn’t able to do it before the midterms, but he has another window here to try and do it before the next presidential. Harris: Michael, I want to talk about the spending. Trump’s super PAC has spent nearly a quarter-billion dollars to help Republicans this election cycle. What do we know about where the president is spending now in this last week, and why is he spending in those spaces? Scherer: So the president, he claims that he will spend $400 million, and that includes some money—it’s on his C4, his dark-money side; we don’t have easy ways of tracking it when all is said and done—which is an enormous amount of money. This is basically additive money that didn’t exist in other cycles. Presidents don’t usually raise money separately to do this. And so the result has been, in the key Senate races around the country, something like 30 or 40 percent more spending on the Republican side than on the Democratic side, all-in. Now, that doesn’t translate to 30, 40 percent more ads, because Democratic candidates are raising more money and candidates get to pay less money for their ads. So every outside dollar that comes in has to pay a different rate than the candidate has to pay. In the House races, it’s closer to even. There’s a slight Republican edge, but again, Democratic candidates tend to be raising more, so on points, they’re doing better. There’s differences in spending by race, but those seem to be intentional strategic differences; different parties have different places. There’s not a huge margin there. In terms of how the president is spending his money, there was concern—we reported back in August—concern that he was gonna spend all this money on himself. And it’s true: He has spent a portion of the money on ads about how great he is, which is not something Republicans wanna see. It’s something Democrats love to see. It really doesn’t clearly affect in positive way these races. That message works if you narrowcast it to Trump supporters. It doesn’t really work on broadcast TV when Trump is polling at 30 percent in the state. But in terms of the other spending, you can’t really separate the Trump spending from the ecosystem spending, and that’s because it’s all being coordinated. So what the Senate Leadership Fund, Congressional Leadership Fund, those are the outside groups tied to the Republican leaders in Congress; what Elon Musk is spending—all of that’s being coordinated. And so they’re basically divvying it up amongst themselves and operating as a single unit. So to say, Well, the president’s priorities are here, and other people’s priorities are there —with the exception of that money that he spent on his own vanity ads, it’s all part of a single strategy. Harris: Thinking about the spending from Musk, the spending from the president, the spending from the various PACs that are out there, spending from candidates themselves, Bloomberg sort of giving $80 million to Democrats. The money is becoming almost exorbitant to the point of nonsensical. And I wonder: Does having more money at this point even really matter? Parker: The airwaves, at the end of the day, can get saturated. In terms of TV broadcast, at the end of the day, there is a finite amount of ads you can buy. And if you’re traveling to cover a race, and you are in Maine, or you are in Iowa, or you are in Texas, it is possible you turn on the TV and all you see are political ads. Gone are the somewhat sketchy prescription-drug ads, and it’s just candidate ads. But I think the money does matter. If you look at how much money they’re pouring into Texas to help prop up a pretty mediocre Republican Senate candidate in Ken Paxton, there is a sense that if if Elon Musk had not put in the money he did, if Trump had not put in the money he did, that Ken Paxton would be floundering. And it’s also an open question about: If they weren’t putting all that money into Texas, could that money be more helpful in some of these other states that are close? So I think at the end of the day, money still matters tremendously. Scherer: The political science on this is that if two sides spend roughly equal amounts of money, they kinda cancel each other out. And generally, that’s true, unless you have new information being presented in the ads that really changes people’s mind, and I think that’s why you’ve seen a lot of data-center ads. It’s new information that’s being added to some of these races, and that’s mostly benefited Democrats. What’s interesting is the late spending. So, the Senate Leadership Fund had just bought a bunch more ads, and they were buying ads in Mississippi, Kansas, South Carolina, and Nebraska—all deep-red states. There wasn’t very large sums of money, but that’s a situation where they’ve seen things in their polling that has made them panic at the late stage. They’re diverting money into deep-red areas, and I think spending in places where there is not a lot of spending, or where people aren’t used to it, could have a better, bigger effect. The real thing Republicans are after right now is not persuasion; it’s turnout. So that’s the other question here. There’s a lot of advertising that’s going on TV, but there’s also a lot of advertising that the Trump team is doing, for instance, on Facebook, using the list they have of Trump voters saying, Y ou really have to get out to vote. Go vote; go vote; go vote. A lot of the Elon Musk–spending is that. All the polling we have says those voters don’t wanna vote right now. They’re just not as excited as they were in 2024. But if they’ve found a new magic formula to do that, and that turns up on Election Day, it could have an impact. Harris: Is that also why you’re seeing the president go and host these sort of boots-on-the-ground rallies in these really deep-ruby-red states, where people might say, Your energies may be spent better elsewhere , in states where races are more competitive? Parker: That is precisely why. I was with the president in Grand Island, Nebraska, which is a very rural part, and red part, of an already red state. And it seemed confusing. At first, the thinking was Trump is just going on a glory days tour. He just likes the adulation and these are places he can go. And that’s all true. He does like the adulation. But in talking to his advisers, they say they track the numbers before he goes into the state and when he leaves, and those trips are all about turnout. Because you have to keep in mind that the Trump coalition that got him elected was a very unlikely coalition of people who specifically liked him, and so that’s why you see him saying, Pretend that I’m on the ballot. And those are people who don’t regularly vote in presidential elections, let alone in off-year midterms. And so, if Trump coming to your city and you standing in line and going to a rally can make you remember to mail in your ballot or go early or show up on Election Day, they believe that’s worth it. Scherer: The problem is that if you’re in a state like Nebraska or Kansas, more than half the people are Trump supporters, naturally. If you’re in a state where it’s less than half, and only 30 percent of the people approve of Trump at this moment—which is a lot of states right now—and he says, Pretend I’m on the ballot, that means something very different for the 70 percent who don’t like him and the 30 percent who like him. So there’s a risk to that. Really what they wanna be doing is narrowcasting that message just to the hardcore believers. Parker: Right. They don’t wanna turn out Democrats. Scherer: But Trump doesn’t always get that nuance and is not convinced that he needs to be cautious. Harris: And actually, to that point—where it could turn out Democrats—we are seeing in the early turnout numbers that they’re outpacing 2018, outpacing 2022 in places like Georgia and among Latino voters overall, who are largely dissatisfied. That coalition that the president had built in 2024 is deteriorating to an extent, if the poll numbers are taken at face value. And historically Democrats vote early; Republicans typically vote day. What are we learning from the early-voting numbers at the moment? Scherer: I have a rule I adopted after the 2020 or 2016 race to never count early-vote numbers to mean anything. And the reason is that, like you said, different populations vote at different rates. Every election is very different. Midterms are very different from presidentials, and every district is reporting their own early votes. And so what you end up getting is like this barrage of numbers. It is clear that Democrats right now are voting with more enthusiasm and higher numbers than the past, but I don’t know what that means. Those Republicans can still go to the polls on Election Day. It doesn’t mean they’re not gonna vote. So I don’t know what any of it means. You just can’t. If person X has not yet voted, you don’t know whether they’re going to vote. And that’s the problem with relying too heavily on the early-voting numbers. Parker: And good campaigns have lists and rolls that tell them person X hasn’t voted yet but probably supports you. So there’s a world in which, three days before Election Day, they get a phone call from their neighbor, and the knock on the door from the canvas, and someone from their church offering to drive them to the polls. So I’m with Michael. Harris: When we come back, we discuss the issues driving voters to the polls. [ Music ] Harris: We’ve talked a lot about the logistics of the campaign, but I wanna get into some of these issues too. We know that affordability is troubling Americans. There was an AP story that I was reading where they were talking about the F-series truck, the F-150, and it’s the most purchased car in America, and it has been for some while. And right now, it costs about $100 to fill up a Ford F-150. That’s about $30 more than it was in 2025. So it’s the affordability issue in a nutshell there. And then you have the Iran war that’s really unpopular with voters as well. As we’ve reported, the president is considering another escalation in the Middle East. What is the play there? Why is the president considering this sort of reescalation in Iran when it is already a deeply unpopular war with voters? Scherer: The play is not a political play. There’s no political advantage to what he’s doing. The Republican campaign this cycle was always gonna be about prices. They had a playbook in February. It was blown up by the Iran war. Since then, you can track the president’s popularity in the generic ballot, which is, Do you plan to vote for a Republican or a Democrat in your congressional race by the price of gas? If gas goes up, Democrats do better, Trump does worse, and reverse. And gas became very expensive in September, which totally explains the drop in polls. It’s gotten slightly better since then. It’s not a lot better, but it’s not getting worse, at least right now. What’s going on in Iran is you have a combination of Israel about to have an election, and Benjamin Netanyahu, the prime minister there, clearly wanting to amp up the idea of a conflict that Trump has to deal with. You have the Houthis continuing to attack places. You have U.S. intelligence saying diplomats in the region are unsafe, and so they’re having to evacuate people. And you have the president, who’s tried for weeks now to say, We’re gonna deal with this, but we’re gonna deal with this after the midterm, which is the politically sound thing to do. The problem is that the Iranians know the same thing. And the best leverage they have right now over the president, barring whatever they’re gonna do if there’s another attack by the U.S., is to weaken him in the midterms. Parker: And politically, the reason it’s such a problem for the president and Republicans is that people aren’t happy about affordability. People—independently of affordability—are unhappy about the war in Iran. Because you may recall, one of the key things Donald Trump promised was no more forever wars, no more quagmires in the Middle East, et cetera, et cetera. And the war in Iran, which people already don’t like on its merit, is so deeply tied with gas prices in a way that people can make that one-to-one connection. So it’s just a nest of what everyone hates. Harris: As we mentioned throughout, the stakes of this are, are kind of clear. If Democrats win back control of the House and the Senate, Trump would be a lame-duck president. He would likely be subject to investigations. We saw, before the House left, even a Republican introduced impeachment, articles of impeachment, against Pete Hegseth. If you were to open your reporter’s notebooks, what are some of the things that you will be thinking about and looking for from the president and the administration, and from Democrats as well, in the last couple of days? Parker: So two things. I think on the investigations front you’re absolutely right. That is the biggest reason Donald Trump wants Republicans to win—is because he wants to shield himself and his staff from what will be myriad investigations. But I think one thing on the Democratic side is there is a risk of overreach. Remember, this is an affordability election. So there is a risk that Democrats can potentially go too far in their investigations in trying to impeach everyone. So that’s a debate the Democrat caucus will have to have themselves. I’m also interested—there is this sense that if Democrats retake control of both chambers of Congress, that Congress will finally again be a check on Donald Trump because Republicans have fundamentally abdicated that role. But my counterintuitive take is: I just don’t know how realistic that is. If Democrats win, especially in the Senate, it is not going to be by huge margins. It is going to be incredibly tight, and Donald Trump has mastered the art and the willingness of doing things without congressional approval, in the face of congressional approval, through executive orders, and other creative levers of power, and sort of saying, I’m gonna smash through everything until a court or someone stops me . Harris: And once it’s broken, it’s harder to put back together. Parker: Right. Once you’ve taken a wrecking ball to the East Wing and a court ruling says you weren’t allowed to do it—well? So I am skeptical of how effective Congress may be in Trump’s last two years if he chooses to try to bulldoze them. Scherer: Trump needs money from Congress. He’s gotta pay for this war; he’s gotta fund his government. The more Democrats in power, the harder that is for him to get his priorities. They’re gonna have more leverage over him. He’s gonna have to eventually bend on some things. But it’s so remarkable, over the last two years, how much has changed and how little of it has had anything to do with legislation. There was one tax bill—the last major piece of legislation they passed, which was a housing affordability bill—he wouldn’t even sign, because he was so disinterested in it. It was a bipartisan bill. So the investigations will matter. They’ll fill the news cycle. There’ll be more disclosures. That sets the stage for 2028. But Trump did not have a legislative plan for the last two years. Parker: It’s not like he’s Obama trying to pass the Affordable Care Act, and you need to really lift it through Congress. Harris: There’s not some big omnibus legislation. Parker: Yeah, exactly. Scherer: And what he has is foreign policy. There’s something [that’s] gonna happen in Cuba in the next six months. He has his building projects, his hometown hobbyist stuff. He’s got the Olympics coming up. He’s got tariffs still he can play with, and he has an ability to pick fights all the time that have nothing to do with legislation, which he’ll continue to do. Harris: So cementing his legacy is more about the things that he can build and the things that he can put together as opposed to– Parker: Yeah, like the physical monuments to himself, rather than the legislation that lives on after him. Harris: Well, Michael, Ashley, thank you so much for giving us so much to think about and helping us understand the last couple of the days before the election better. Parker: Thank you. Scherer: Thanks for having us. Harris: That’s all for today’s show. This episode of Radio Atlantic was produced by Mike Pesoli and edited by Hadley Robinson. It was engineered by Miguel Carrascal and has original music by Rob Smierciak. Claudine Ebeid is the executive producer of Atlantic podcasts, and Andrea Valdez is our managing editor. If you like what you saw here, new episodes of Radio Atlantic drop every Monday and Thursday. You can subscribe on The Atlantic ’s YouTube page, on Apple or Spotify, or wherever it is you get your podcasts. And if you want to support this work and the work of my colleagues, you can subscribe to the publication at TheAtlantic.com/Listener. Until next time, I’m Adam Harris.

items.title: Anthropic files for IPO, reveals soaring revenue, massive net losses
items.description: US artificial intelligence (AI) company Anthropic publicly filed its prospectus for an initial public offering (IPO) on Monday, which could become the largest stock market debut in history. The filing, a registration statement on Form S-1 with the US Securities and Exchange Commission, did not set the number of shares to be sold or a price range. Anthropic intends to list its Class A common stock on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the ticker symbol ANT, according to a release on the company's website. Both the company and existing shareholders will sell shares, with Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley named first among 24 underwriters. The company is expected to begin trading in mid-November, and backers hope for a valuation of up to $2 trillion, though some investors have weighed a figure closer to $1.5 trillion, according to Reuters. The prospectus offers the first detailed look at the finances of the developer of the Claude AI models. Revenues reached $16.29 billion in the first half of 2026, up from $1.16 billion year on year, after growing from $41 million in 2023 to $386 million in 2024 and $4.59 billion in 2025. Revenues in the second quarter alone were $11.56 billion, and the company reported its first quarterly operating profit of $974 million. The headline losses are far larger, but most stem from accounting charges rather than cash spending. Anthropic recorded a net loss of $80.7 billion in the first half of 2026, of which $72.4 billion came from changes in the fair value of convertible notes and other instruments as the company's own valuation climbed. Its operating loss for the period was $693 million, while operating cash flow turned positive at $3.93 billion. Cash and short-term investments totaled $131.7 billion at June 30. The filing warns that this rapid pace may not last. "We cannot assure you [revenue] will continue to grow at all," the company said in the prospectus, which also notes it is on track for a second consecutive quarter of adjusted operating profit. Spending on computing power remains the central cost. Anthropic spent nearly $9 billion on computing resources and infrastructure in the first half of 2026, and has committed to $518 billion in future infrastructure spending. It has agreed to spend at least $110 billion with Amazon through April 2036 and at least $114.5 billion with Google through July 2033. Amazon holds $6.2 billion of notes that convert into non-voting stock, capped at 12% of the company. By September 30, more than 1,900 customers generated at least $1 million each in trailing annual revenue, and more than 11,900 generated at least $100,000, up from 950 a year earlier. Existing customers spend roughly nine times what they did a year ago, but two unnamed customers accounted for about 23% of revenues in the first half of 2026. Public investors will be able to buy the shares but will not steer the company. A single Class F share held by the seven co-founders carries 50.1% of every stockholder vote, and a trust will elect a majority of the board. A Public Benefit Fund will hold 5% of the company in non-voting shares, and each co-founder has pledged to give 80% of their personal Anthropic equity to philanthropic causes. The prospectus devotes sections to risk factors, including warnings that advanced AI could pose "catastrophic or existential risks to humanity" and that liability from extreme harm could exceed what any insurer can cover. Anthropic raised $65 billion in May at a $965-billion valuation. A debut above $2 trillion would surpass SpaceX's $1.77-trillion listing in June, the current record. Reuters has reported Anthropic's third-quarter revenue of $16.8 billion and forward projections pointing to revenue of about $190 billion to $200 billion in 2028.

USA : une sénatrice de 82 ans inculpée pour gestion d’un réseau de trafic de marijuana
items.description: Les procureurs fédéraux ont arrêté une figure politique majeure de Virginie, aux Etats-Unis, accusée d’avoir dirigé une entreprise criminelle de trafic de marijuana. La sénatrice d’État démocrate L. Louise Lucas, âgée de 82 ans, ainsi que six autres personnes, dont des membres de sa famille, ont été inculpées dans le cadre d’une vaste affaire de racket impliquant présumément des faits de fraude, d’infractions à la législation sur les stupéfiants et de corruption. Selon les documents judiciaires, elle fait face à cinq chefs d’accusation pour crimes ( felonies ) : association de malfaiteurs en vue de commettre un racket ( racketeering conspiracy ), association de malfaiteurs en vue de distribuer de la marijuana, complot en vue de blanchir de l’argent, association de malfaiteurs en vue de commettre une fraude aux services honnêtes ( honest services fraud ), et tenue d’un local utilisé pour le trafic de drogue. Les deux filles de la femme politique ainsi que son petit-fils figurent parmi les co-conspirateurs présumés. Selon la plainte déposée auprès du tribunal fédéral du district est de Virginie, Mme Lucas et au moins six autres associés « étaient membres et affiliés de la Lucas Enterprise , une organisation criminelle qui s’adonnait, entre autres, à des ententes en vue de distribuer et de détenir de la marijuana avec l’intention de la distribuer ». Mme Lucas, présidente pro tempore du Sénat de Virginie, a publié une réaction sur les réseaux sociaux le jeudi 22 octobre : « Aujourd’hui, le FBI, le ministère de la Justice et toute la puissance du gouvernement fédéral ont été déployés contre une arrière-grand-mère de 82 ans. J’ai grandi sous le régime des lois Jim Crow. J’ai vu ce qui arrive lorsque les personnes au pouvoir tentent de faire taire ceux qui leur tiennent tête. J’ai passé ma vie à me battre, et ce n’est pas aujourd’hui que je vais m’arrêter. Ce n’est pas nouveau pour moi, c’est le combat de ma vie. Je ne me laisserai pas intimider. Je ne me laisserai pas persécuter. Et je ne céderai pas. » Cette arrestation intervient alors que les forces de l’ordre fédérales poursuivent leurs enquêtes ciblant des opposants politiques du président. Le procureur général des États-Unis, Todd Blanche, a nié que le dossier de Mme Lucas soit à caractère politique. « Nous sommes ici aujourd’hui en raison de faits et de preuves qui ont amené cette enquête à débuter il y a de nombreuses années, ainsi que de faits et de preuves qui ont conduit le grand jury à inculper la sénatrice Lucas et ses co-conspirateurs présumés », a-t-il déclaré. « Et ce sont les faits et les preuves qui continueront de guider nos procureurs fédéraux dans cette affaire. » L’Associated Press a rapporté en mai qu’une enquête pénale visant Mme Lucas avait débuté sous l’administration du président démocrate Joe Biden. M. Blanche a précisé que l’enquête avait commencé « bien avant la réélection du président Trump ». « Nous ne faisons pas de règlements de comptes politiques », a ajouté M. Blanche. L’article USA : une sénatrice de 82 ans inculpée pour gestion d’un réseau de trafic de marijuana est apparu en premier sur NetAfrique.net .

items.title: Reconstruction post-séisme Al Haouz : Les ressources du fonds spécial détaillées dans le PLF 2027
items.description: Le fonds spécial consacré à la gestion des conséquences du séisme qui a frappé le Maroc poursuit le financement des opérations de reconstruction et de réhabilitation des zones sinistrées. Dans un rapport annexé au projet de loi de finances (PLF) pour 2027, le gouvernement dresse le bilan des ressources mobilisées, des aides distribuées aux ménages et des chantiers engagés, tout en détaillant les opérations dont l’achèvement est attendu en 2027. Au 15 septembre 2026, les aides directes versées par l’État aux ménages sinistrés, par l’intermédiaire de la Caisse nationale de retraite et d’assurances (CNRA), ont atteint environ 8,108 milliards de dirhams. Cet organisme est chargé de gérer les aides et de les mettre à la disposition de leurs bénéficiaires. Les dépenses du fonds spécial se sont élevées à 19,71 milliards de dirhams en 2023, pour des ressources de 20,71 milliards de dirhams. En 2024, les ressources ont atteint 12,18 milliards de dirhams, contre 8,62 milliards de dépenses. En 2025, elles se sont établies à 6,05 milliards de dirhams, tandis que les dépenses ont totalisé 2,39 milliards de dirhams. Des aides différenciées selon les dégâts subis Le dispositif d’aide aux ménages repose sur plusieurs catégories de soutien, en fonction de la nature des dommages occasionnés par le séisme. Les aides d’urgence mensuelles, fixées à 2 500 dirhams, ont bénéficié à 63 135 ménages, pour un montant cumulé de 2,531 milliards de dirhams. Pour les logements entièrement effondrés, l’État a accordé une aide directe de 140 000 dirhams par ménage. Au total, 5 741 ménages en ont bénéficié, pour une enveloppe de 765,46 millions de dirhams, versée en quatre tranches. Les ménages dont les logements ont subi des dommages nécessitant une réhabilitation ont, pour leur part, reçu une aide de 80.000 dirhams. Selon le rapport, 52 256 ménages ont bénéficié de ce dispositif, pour un montant global de 4,006 milliards de dirhams. Le programme a également été étendu aux ménages résidant à l’intérieur des remparts de l’ancienne médina de Marrakech, qui ne sont pas propriétaires des logements endommagés. Au 31 août 2026, 326 ménages avaient bénéficié d’une aide directe de 80 000 dirhams, sous réserve de remplir les conditions prévues. Les frais de gestion facturés à l’État par la CNRA au titre des deux programmes d’aides précités s’élevaient à 10,96 millions de dirhams au 15 septembre 2026. 6,424 milliards de dirhams pour les infrastructures publiques Au-delà des aides aux particuliers, le fonds finance la remise en état des infrastructures et des équipements publics endommagés. Les financements mobilisés pour les interventions d’urgence pilotées par les départements ministériels ont atteint 6,424 milliards de dirhams au 15 septembre 2026. Les opérations engagées couvrent un large éventail de chantiers : consolidation et reconstruction de sites et de monuments historiques, réparation des routes endommagées, déblaiement des décombres de bâtiments abritant des services publics ou des établissements d’enseignement, remise en état des ouvrages hydrauliques et des réseaux de distribution d’eau potable. Le programme comprend également la reconstruction et la réhabilitation des établissements scolaires et des centres de santé considérés comme prioritaires. D’après le rapport, la majorité de ces opérations est entrée dans sa phase finale. Leur poursuite s’inscrit dans le cadre du programme d’urgence destiné à réhabiliter les zones touchées par le séisme. Des plateformes de stockage et le plan de développement du Haut Atlas Le fonds contribue également au financement de projets destinés à renforcer les capacités de stockage des produits de première nécessité. Les crédits mobilisés pour la réalisation, l’équipement et la mise en service des plateformes régionales de stockage ont atteint environ 4,3 milliards de dirhams au 15 septembre 2026. Les fonds nécessaires doivent être débloqués en fonction de l’avancement des travaux. Parallèlement, l’Agence de développement du Haut Atlas a bénéficié d’une enveloppe de 928,6 millions de dirhams prélevée sur les ressources du fonds, afin de financer son plan d’action pour les années 2025 et 2026. Ce montant était mobilisé à la même date, le 15 septembre 2026. La reconstruction se poursuivra en 2027 Le PLF pour 2027 prévoit la poursuite des travaux de reconstruction et de réhabilitation des infrastructures endommagées, ainsi que le financement du plan d’action de l’Agence de développement du Haut Atlas et l’achèvement du chantier des plateformes régionales de stockage des produits de première nécessité. Parmi les opérations programmées figure l’achèvement de la réhabilitation d’un tronçon de la route nationale n° 7, sur une longueur de 64 kilomètres. Le programme prévoit également la poursuite de l’accompagnement des commerçants dont les locaux ont été endommagés par le séisme. Enfin, les travaux de réhabilitation des édifices religieux et des bâtiments relevant des Habous touchés par le séisme doivent être menés à leur terme. À travers ces différents volets, le rapport annexé au PLF 2027 met en évidence la poursuite d’un programme qui associe aides financières aux ménages, remise en état des équipements publics et reconstruction des infrastructures, avec plusieurs opérations encore attendues au cours de l’année à venir. The post Reconstruction post-séisme Al Haouz : Les ressources du fonds spécial détaillées dans le PLF 2027 appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Jaou Tunis | Charles Brecard présente son solo primé « Il pleut, il plaint, il rage » au 4ème Art
items.description: Dans le cadre de la biennale Jaou Tunis, le chorégraphe et interprète Charles Brecard présente son solo, « Il pleut, il plaint, il rage », une œuvre intense pensée comme un voyage intime et un exutoire salvateur face aux absurdités du monde moderne. Cette pièce a valu à son auteur le premier prix de la meilleure chorégraphie lors du prestigieux festival Internationales Solo Tanz Theater Stuttgart en 2023. Fort de ce succès international, le projet a ensuite bénéficié de deux résidences de création en Italie, au sein des compagnies Dance Arts Faculty et Equilibrio Dynamico, permettant d'affiner une gestuelle singulière et profondément expressive. Conçu comme une quête de réconfort à travers le mouvement, ce spectacle invite le public à une traversée émotionnelle brute et captivante. Une création majeure de la programmation de Jaou Tunis à ne pas manquer ce lundi 26 octobre à 19h sur les planches du 4ème Art.
